quotes.heading: Improving our coverage of travel and tourism statistics
quotes.quote: The methodological approach to IPS sampling changed notably when the new survey design was introduced in July 2024. Sampling at airports was moved from a terminal-basis to a route-basis, an approach that aligns with producing more precise statistics at individual country level.

quotes.heading: UK-level estimates
quotes.quote: From 1 April 2024, IPS data collection in Northern Ireland (NI) stopped. Data on international tourism to and from NI are now provided by the Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (NISRA). Our Travel trends: 2024 article and our Travel trends: 2025 article include UK-level world totals in their headline estimates only. The remaining estimates and breakdowns cover Great Britain-level geographies only, and our quarterly tables continue to cover the Great Britain-level only.

quotes.heading: How these figures can be used
quotes.quote: The results remain preliminary and are likely to change as more data are collected under the new design, and as the time series modelling framework develops. They do not represent final discontinuity estimates or an agreed method for adjusting historical series.

quotes.heading: 1. Main points
quotes.quote: Quarter 1 (Jan to Mar) and Quarter 2 (Apr to June) 2024 data were collected and produced under our previous International Passenger Survey (IPS) design, while Quarter 3 (July to Sept) and Quarter 4 (Oct to Dec) 2024 data were collected and produced under our new IPS design; this may lead to discontinuities between the two halves of 2024 and affects how the data should be used.
